baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction 'they fear their Lord bi-l-ghayb' joins khashyah, lordship, and concealment from sight.
baseline_models.mechanism: Awe-bearing fear sustains answerability to the sovereign Lord where neither the Lord nor the promised consequence is directly visible.

activation_trace.role: Fear together with awe supplies a reverential rather than merely alarmed posture.
Lordship, ownership, and sovereignty make the fear relational and answerable.
Concealment from eyes supplies the condition in which reverence persists without direct sight.

changed_reading.before: A general promise to people who fear their Lord.
changed_reading.after: A promise to people whose reverent accountability remains active without direct sight of the Lord or outcome.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Bi-l-ghayb can describe the worshippers' hidden or socially unobserved condition as well as an unseen object.
baseline_models.mechanism: The same fear that could be displayed publicly remains operative in absence and concealment, making private integrity the diagnostic feature.

activation_trace.role: Awe-bearing fear names the inward restraint that continues when display is unavailable.
Being concealed from eyes supports a circumstantial reading of acting while unobserved.
The branch of speaking about a person in that person's absence preserves a specifically social sense of absence.

changed_reading.before: The unseen is only the content believed or feared.
changed_reading.after: The unseen also names the unobserved setting in which the person's relation to the Lord proves genuine.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The result is paired as maghfirah and a great ajr.
baseline_models.mechanism: The promise first covers liability and protects its bearer from the consequence of fault, then adds a positive return whose magnitude is enlarged.

activation_trace.role: Covering sin and shielding its bearer from its effect supplies the reparative first term.
Recompense for work supplies a positive return beyond cancellation of liability.
Magnitude opposed to smallness marks the return as ample rather than merely adequate.

changed_reading.before: Forgiveness and reward are two near-synonymous benefits.
changed_reading.after: The verse promises a two-stage outcome: protection from the residue of fault and then an abundant positive recompense.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Rabb can carry repair, gradual completion, nourishment, and growth alongside sovereignty.
baseline_models.mechanism: The relation to 'their Lord' can be developmental: the one feared with awe is also the one who tends beings toward completion, making the great reward a matured outcome rather than an external prize alone.

activation_trace.role: Repair, nurture, and completion supply gradual formative lordship.
The split mapped branch of feeding and growth makes cultivation a live but form-distant image.
Great magnitude supplies the enlarged result of that developmental process.

changed_reading.before: The Lord judges and pays a large reward.
changed_reading.after: The Lord also tends a hidden disposition toward completion until its outcome becomes great.

context_deltas.mechanism: The life-and-death test is defined as making the quality of intentional work appear; reverence in an unobserved condition becomes the hidden quality that the test discloses and reward answers.

activation_trace.role: Concealment supplies the condition in which quality is not yet publicly visible.
Testing that makes a condition appear turns hidden reverence into diagnostic evidence.
Intentional action links the inward posture to conduct whose quality can be tested.

structural_cues: 67:2 places death, life, testing, best action, and forgiveness in one sequence before the focus promise.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: testing reveals a condition and work is intentional action. Reader arrow: unobserved conditions expose the quality later answered by reward. Live alternative: the test and bi-l-ghayb may remain adjacent rather than causally linked.

changed_reading.before: Private fear is simply one commendable state.
changed_reading.after: Private reverence is the test condition that reveals the quality of a person's intentional life.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated visual inspection is demanded and then reaches its own limit; bi-l-ghayb therefore begins beyond disciplined sight rather than in refusal to look.

activation_trace.role: What is concealed from eyes anchors the focus phrase at the boundary of visual access.
Eye-sight and insight supply the demanded act of inspection before any appeal to the unseen.
Repeated eyesight makes the sensory procedure explicit and sustained.
Exhausted, spent capacity marks the point at which sight can go no farther.

structural_cues: 67:3-4 twice returns the gaze to creation and ends with that gaze humbled and exhausted.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: sight is repeated until its power is spent. Reader arrow: the focus commends reverence on the far side of that sensory limit, not credulity before inspection. Live alternative: the sight sequence may establish creation's integrity without defining bi-l-ghayb.

changed_reading.before: Fear of the unseen contrasts with empirical looking.
changed_reading.after: Reverence in the unseen is what remains warranted after looking has been exercised rigorously and has reached its limit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The condemned finally understand and confess only after the threatened reality is present; the focus praises the inverse timing, an inward acknowledgment that governs action before disclosure becomes coercive.

activation_trace.role: Awe-bearing fear supplies anticipatory restraint rather than retrospective panic.
Concealment locates that restraint before the outcome is made present.
Hearing as understanding and compliance identifies the response the speakers say they lacked.
Reason that restrains from ignorance supplies the missed preventive faculty.
Confession and yielding show recognition arriving after prevention is no longer possible.
Sin supplies the liability that late confession can name but no longer avert.

structural_cues: 67:10 is a counterfactual about listening and reasoning; 67:11 follows with confession, then 67:12 opens with a contrasting rewarded group.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: failed understanding is followed by late confession, then the focus praises unseen reverence. Reader arrow: the focus describes voluntary pre-disclosure accountability. Live alternative: the adjacency may mark only two populations, not two timings of recognition.

changed_reading.before: The verse rewards belief in an unseen reality.
changed_reading.after: The verse rewards acknowledging accountability early enough for it to govern conduct, before undeniable disclosure forces confession.

context_deltas.mechanism: Secret and public speech are placed on the same epistemic plane before the Creator who knows the interior source of action; bi-l-ghayb becomes hidden from human observers but never hidden from the Lord.

activation_trace.role: Concealment from eyes anchors the private side of the focus construction.
Hiding something inward supplies the private mode that follows the focus verse.
Public declaration and raised voice provide the explicit control case for secrecy.
The interior origin from which actions issue moves the contrast beneath speech to motive.
Knowledge of the inward reality closes any gap between social invisibility and divine knowledge.

structural_cues: 67:13 immediately follows the focus by pairing concealed and public speech; 67:14 grounds knowledge in creation itself.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: secrecy, publicity, the action-producing interior, and knowledge of inner reality are juxtaposed. Reader arrow: bi-l-ghayb describes integrity outside human surveillance but inside divine knowledge. Live alternative: it may primarily describe fear of the unseen Lord rather than the worshipper's privacy.

changed_reading.before: They fear in a zone where nothing is seen.
changed_reading.after: They remain reverent when no human sees them precisely because their hidden interior is not unknown to their Lord.

context_deltas.mechanism: Tractable fertile earth, allotted nourishment, and revival imagery activate the developmental branches of Rabb; the great reward can be pictured as the ripened outcome of a disposition cultivated out of sight.

activation_trace.role: Nurture and completion make lordship an ongoing formative relation.
The split branch of feeding and growth supplies the latent cultivation image.
Soft, fertile earth supplies the receptive material in which hidden development can occur.
Nourishing sustenance supplies what maintains the developmental process.
Dried pasture revived by rain supplies an ecological image for a later disclosed outcome.

structural_cues: 67:15 joins a made-tractable earth, walking, eating provision, and eventual emergence in a single movement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: earth is receptive, provision nourishes, and n-sh-r includes rain-revival. Reader arrow: Rabb cultivates unseen reverence until it matures as great reward. Live alternative: 67:15 may concern use and resurrection without implying moral cultivation.

changed_reading.before: A sovereign gives an externally assigned reward.
changed_reading.after: A nurturing Lord brings a hidden disposition to maturity, and its greatness is also the scale of what has been cultivated.

context_deltas.mechanism: Visible wings spread and contract, yet their continued flight is assigned to an unseen holding by the Merciful; the unseen object of khashyah is therefore sustaining agency as well as possible threat.

activation_trace.role: Awe-bearing fear can answer dependence and majesty without requiring a threatening object.
Concealment from sight allows the sustaining cause to remain unseen behind visible motion.
Contraction after extension describes the visible alternation of the birds' wings.
Holding and restraining supplies the invisible support beneath that visible alternation.
Mercy and tenderness identify the hidden holder as beneficent rather than only dangerous.

structural_cues: 67:19 moves from observable wing positions to the assertion that none holds the birds except the Merciful.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: wing contraction is visible, holding is assigned to Mercy, and the focus names unseen awe. Reader arrow: khashyah responds to hidden sustaining dependence, not only hidden punishment. Live alternative: the bird scene may illustrate power independently of the focus emotion.

changed_reading.before: They fear a threat concealed in the unseen.
changed_reading.after: They stand in awe of the unseen sustaining mercy on which every visible motion depends.

context_deltas.mechanism: A promise whose timing is questioned becomes abruptly near and seen; bi-l-ghayb gains a temporal force, naming the interval in which one responds before deferred disclosure arrives.

activation_trace.role: Absence from present sight supplies the current condition of the promised outcome.
An appointment locates fulfillment in a not-yet-reached time and sharpens temporal deferral.
The rush into nearness reverses the prior distance of the promised event.
Actual seeing marks the endpoint of the interval called unseen in the focus reading.

structural_cues: 67:25 asks when the promise will occur; 67:27 answers narratively with the moment it is seen as near.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: a timed promise moves from questioned delay to nearness and sight. Reader arrow: the focus praises response during the delay, before sight compels it. Live alternative: ghayb may remain spatial or epistemic rather than temporal.

changed_reading.before: The unseen is a fixed invisible realm.
changed_reading.after: The unseen is also a temporary interval before a deferred reality comes near and becomes visible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing confession joins faith, reliance, and the Merciful; this relational field recalibrates khashyah as lucid awe compatible with settled trust, not destabilizing panic.

activation_trace.role: Fear joined with awe leaves room for reverence without panic.
Mercy and tenderness qualify the character of the Lord toward whom the focus directs awe.
Belief that brings the heart tranquility supplies settled assent alongside fear.
Reliance supplies active entrustment to the same unseen Lord.

structural_cues: 67:29 names the Merciful, then coordinates belief in him with reliance upon him.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: mercy, heart-settling belief, and reliance coexist near the focus's khashyah. Reader arrow: these cues constrain fear away from panic toward reverent dependence. Live alternative: the emotional tones may coexist without one defining the other.

changed_reading.before: Fear and trust pull in opposite directions.
changed_reading.after: Khashyah is the vigilant side of the same relationship whose settled side is faith and reliance on the Merciful.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing water question contrasts an indispensable resource sunk beyond reach with water visibly issuing from a spring; the low-place branch of ghayb becomes a material model of dependence on support that can disappear from access.

activation_trace.role: A depression in which a thing disappears gives hiddenness a downward, inaccessible spatial form.
Water's appearance and abundance define the accessible support that the question places at risk.
Descent into depth supplies the mechanism by which necessary support passes out of reach.
A flowing water source supplies the visible, reachable reversal of withdrawal into depth.

structural_cues: 67:30 closes the surah by opposing water gone into depth to water brought as an accessible flowing source.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: water can descend beyond reach or issue visibly from a source; ghayb includes a low place where things disappear. Reader arrow: unseen reverence recognizes dependence even while support is accessible. Live alternative: the water question may concern provision without redefining bi-l-ghayb.

changed_reading.before: The unseen is primarily an abstract object of belief.
changed_reading.after: The unseen is also the hidden depth from which sustaining gifts come and into which they can withdraw, making reverence an awareness of radical dependence.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because mending a fracture that healed crooked is a technical, form-distant branch of ajr rather than its ordinary recompense sense. It remains anchored to the focus's ء ج ر B002 and is activated by the face-down versus whole-and-upright walking contrast in 67:22. Downstream prose should present it only as a restorative image carried alongside wages, never as a replacement gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus word ajr carries a branch image of setting or mending a fracture on a bend.

activation_trace.role: Mending a fracture that has set crooked supplies a possible restorative dimension to reward.
Being overturned or cast onto the face supplies the damaged orientation requiring repair.
Wholeness and straightness in the self supply the repaired bodily and moral orientation.
Uprightness, balance, and evenness complete the movement from warped collapse to restored gait.

changed_reading.before: The great ajr is payment added after conduct.
changed_reading.after: At the level of a contained branch image, the great ajr may also be the mending that lets a bent, face-down life stand and walk straight.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain botanical activation, surprising because hidden tree roots are not the ordinary gloss of ghayb and sowing is not the surface sense of 67:24. It remains anchored to the packet's غ ي ب B008 plus Rabb's growth branch and is reinforced by earth, sowing, and watering branches. Render it as an exploratory mechanism for inward formation, not as lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Ghayb includes a branch image of tree roots concealed in earth and later exposed by digging, while Rabb has a split feeding-and-growth branch.

activation_trace.role: Hidden tree roots supply an underground model for a disposition whose effects can emerge above visibility.
Feeding and growth assign the Lord a cultivating role in the hidden root system.
Soft, fertile earth supplies the medium that receives and conceals roots.
Sowing land supplies the beginning of growth below the visible surface.
Delivering water by irrigation supplies hidden nourishment for what later emerges.

changed_reading.before: Bi-l-ghayb marks an invisible realm or an unobserved circumstance.
changed_reading.after: As a contained botanical image, unseen reverence is a living root system cultivated below view, nourished by the Lord, and disclosed later in conduct and reward.

strongest_changes: Bi-l-ghayb became both epistemic and social: beyond exhausted sight, yet also private conduct fully known to the Lord.
The verse came to praise accountability before forced disclosure, in contrast with understanding and confession that arrive only after the outcome is present.
The bird and trust sequences revised khashyah away from panic toward awe before sustaining mercy, held together with faith and reliance.
The promise-to-nearness sequence gave hiddenness a temporal dimension: the interval before what is deferred becomes seen.
The final water question gave hiddenness a material depth, exposing dependence on support that can recede beyond access.
summary.what_was_special: The context repeatedly moved between seen and unseen, public and secret, deferred and near, available and withdrawn. Those reversals made the focus verse function less as a static label for believers and more as a portrait of how inward accountability operates before visibility compels it.
remaining_uncertainties: Bi-l-ghayb can still distribute its force among the unseen Lord, unseen consequence, the worshipper's private condition, and the hidden interior; the packet keeps these readings live rather than selecting one.
The cultivation, hidden-root, and mended-fracture models depend on deliberately form-distant branches and should remain images rather than asserted lexical senses.
The water and bird mechanisms may independently illustrate divine provision rather than directly revise the semantics of the focus phrase.
